cases.sentence: Анна Михайловна, узнав (как она и всё знала, что́ делалось в доме) о получении письма, ___ вошла к графу и застала его с письмом в руках рыдающим и вместе смеющимся.
cases.explain: «тихим шагом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: It was long since the Rostóvs had news of Nikolúshka. Not till midwinter was the count at last handed a letter addressed in his son’s handwriting. On receiving it, he ran on tiptoe to his study in alarm and haste, trying to escape notice, closed the door, and began to read the letter. Anna Mikháylovna, who always knew everything that passed in the house, on hearing of the arrival of the letter went softly into the room and found the count with it in his hand, sobbing and laughing at the same time.

cases.sentence: Всякий раз как при этих намеках графиня начинала беспокоиться и тревожно взглядывать то на графа, то на Анну Михайловну, Анна Михайловна самым ___ сводила разговор на незначительные предметы.
cases.explain: «незаметным образом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: At dinner Anna Mikháylovna talked the whole time about the war news and about Nikolúshka, twice asked when the last letter had been received from him, though she knew that already, and remarked that they might very likely be getting a letter from him that day. Each time that these hints began to make the countess anxious and she glanced uneasily at the count and at Anna Mikháylovna, the latter very adroitly turned the conversation to insignificant matters. Natásha, who, of the whole family, was the most gifted with a capacity to feel any shades of intonation, look, and expression, pricked up her ears from the beginning of the meal and was certain that there was some secret between her father and Anna Mikháylovna, that it had something to do with her brother, and that Anna Mikháylovna was preparing them for it. Bold as she was, Natásha, who knew how sensitive her mother was to anything relating to Nikolúshka, did not venture to ask any questions at dinner, but she was too excited to eat anything and kept wriggling about on her chair regardless of her governess’ remarks. After dinner, she rushed headlong after Anna Mikháylovna and, dashing at her, flung herself on her neck as soon as she overtook her in the sitting room.

cases.sentence: — вскрикнула Наташа, прочтя ___ в лице Анны Михайловны.
cases.explain: «утвердительный ответ» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “A letter from Nikólenka! I’m sure of it!” exclaimed Natásha, reading confirmation in Anna Mikháylovna’s face.

cases.sentence: Анна Михайловна в ___ рассказала Наташе содержание письма с условием не говорить никому.
cases.explain: «коротких словах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Anna Mikháylovna, in a few words, told her the contents of the letter, on condition that she should tell no one.

cases.sentence: Наташа, увидав впечатление, произведенное на Соню известием о ране брата, в ___ почувствовала всю горестную сторону этого известия.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Natásha, seeing the impression the news of her brother’s wound produced on Sónya, felt for the first time the sorrowful side of the news.

cases.sentence: — Вот видно, что все вы, женщины, — плаксы, — сказал Петя, решительными ___ прохаживаясь по комнате.
cases.explain: «большими шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “There now! It’s true that all you women are crybabies,” remarked Pétya, pacing the room with large, resolute strides. “Now I’m very glad, very glad indeed, that my brother has distinguished himself so. You are all blubberers and understand nothing.” Natásha smiled through her tears.

cases.explain: «минутного молчания» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Do you remember him?” Natásha suddenly asked, after a moment’s silence. Sónya smiled.

cases.sentence: Теперь, когда он был уже офицер и ___, хорошо ли было с ее стороны напомнить ему о себе и как будто о том обязательстве, которое он взял на себя в отношении ее.
cases.explain: «раненый герой» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Sónya became thoughtful. The question of how to write to Nicolas, and whether she ought to write, tormented her. Now that he was already an officer and a wounded hero, would it be right to remind him of herself and, as it might seem, of the obligations to her he had taken on himself?

cases.sentence: — Не глупее тебя, матушка, — сказал девятилетний Петя, точно как будто он был ___.
cases.explain: «старый бригадир» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Not more stupid than you, madam,” said the nine-year-old Pétya, with the air of an old brigadier.

cases.sentence: Уйдя к себе, она, сидя на кресле, не спускала глаз с ___ сына, вделанного в табакерке, и слезы навертывались ей на глаза.
cases.explain: «миниатюрного портрета» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The countess had been prepared by Anna Mikháylovna’s hints at dinner. On retiring to her own room, she sat in an armchair, her eyes fixed on a miniature portrait of her son on the lid of a snuffbox, while the tears kept coming into her eyes. Anna Mikháylovna, with the letter, came on tiptoe to the countess’ door and paused.
